questions.prompt: Which beginning-of-construction method governs: off-site transformer manufacture starting December 22, 2025, or on-site physical work starting January 12, 2026?
questions.context: The construction start year drives three assumptions. It sets the domestic content threshold (45% for a 2025 start vs 50% for 2026, against an adjusted percentage of 47.8%), and it determines whether the FEOC material assistance rules apply. The independent engineer gives no opinion on the off-site work. The notice to proceed alone is not physical work.

evidence.text: On-site physical work of a significant nature, beginning with pile installation for the tracker foundations, commenced on January 12, 2026.
Physical manufacture of the transformer, beginning with cutting and stacking of the custom core, commenced at our facility on December 22, 2025 and continued thereafter.
We have not reviewed the manufacturer's records and express no opinion on the tax treatment of off-site work.
If construction is determined to have begun in 2026, the applicable threshold would be 50% and the Project would not qualify at the computed adjusted percentage.
No material assistance cost ratio calculation has been prepared.

options.label: Off-site transformer work governs (2025 start)
options.consequence: The domestic content bonus qualifies at 47.8% against the 45% threshold, and the FEOC rules do not apply. Buyer should still require the Seller's memo, manufacturer records and proof of a continuous program of work.

options.label: On-site physical work governs (2026 start)
options.consequence: The domestic content bonus fails because 47.8% is below 50%, so the rate falls to 40% and the credit to $54,560,000 on $136,400,000 basis. The FEOC rules apply, and compliance is unverified without the module certification and a cost ratio calculation.

options.label: Hold open pending Seller's memo and manufacturer records
options.consequence: The domestic content bonus and FEOC status stay unresolved. Make a satisfactory beginning-of-construction opinion a condition precedent to signing.

questions.prompt: How should the unmet apprenticeship labor-hour requirement and the pending $370,800 cure payment be treated?

evidence.text: The labor hour requirement is not satisfied for the period reviewed. The Seller has not documented a Good Faith Effort exception for the shortfall.

options.label: Treat PWA as not met until the cure is paid and evidenced
options.consequence: The term sheet's credit rate is unsupported until payment is proven. Make proof of the $370,800 payment and an updated compliance report a condition precedent to funding.

options.label: Accept Seller's covenant to pay the cure before placed in service, backed by specific indemnity
options.consequence: Buyer keeps the 50% rate assumption but carries uninsured risk, because the insurance exclusion leaves only the Seller/Sponsor indemnity. Proof of payment is still required at funding.
